key_developments: 29 September — the RBA raised the cash rate 25bp to 4.60% with all nine Board members in favour and retained the 'further if needed' sentence; the Australian dollar fell about 0.3% and GBP/AUD rose 161 pips to a cycle-high 1.90991 the following session.

30 September — Australian August CPI at 4.0% against 4.1% expected with the trimmed mean held at 3.6% for a third month removed the November hike extension, and three-year yields fell about 10bp to 4.87%.

28 September — President Trump rejected Iran's seven-day Hormuz reopening plan, reversing last week's de-escalation risk; gold fell 3% to its lowest since 5 August, with XAU/USD down 172 dollars from 4,286.74 to 4,115.08 in one session.
1 October — the euro hit a 17-month low below $1.13 on French yields at a 14-year high, dragging EUR/GBP to 0.85205 and EUR/SGD down 82 pips; the US 10-year reached 5.34%, its highest since 2002.
1 October — Swiss September CPI printed its strongest annual increase since August 2024, comfortably beating a 0.5% consensus; SGD/CHF fell 51 pips and EUR/CHF fell 127 on the day.
2 October — US September payrolls rose only 29,000 with unemployment at 4.2% and prior months revised lower, yet the dollar index held above 102 and GBP/USD recovered just 45 pips.
new_risks_identified: French sovereign stress has become a G10 FX driver in its own right, simultaneously driving the euro to 17-month lows and bidding the franc as a haven — it cuts across Long EUR/GBP, Short EUR/SGD and Long SGD/CHF at once.

The dollar has detached from the policy-rate channel: October Fed hike odds fell from 70.9% to under 40% after soft core inflation and a Williams speech, and the dollar index still cleared 102 on term premium with the 10-year above 5.3%.

Hormuz re-escalation after the 28 September rejection reverses last week's de-escalation risk, supporting the sterling and kiwi terms-of-trade legs but doing nothing for the sterling crosses, where the rate channel now dominates.
The 28 October UK Budget sits seven days before an 85–87%-priced 5 November BoE decision; a Budget-conditioned pause would unwind the sterling cross rally as violently as the hike repriced it.
consensus_shifts: October ECB hike pricing has collapsed from the 75.1% reported on 27 September to 22%, with four euro-area inflation beats on 30 September failing to lift the currency.
5 November BoE hike pricing hardened to 85–87%, with Capital Economics now forecasting 25bp twice more — to 4.00% in November and 4.25% in February.

MAS expectations reversed from a near-consensus hold to a live third tightening on 14 October: 45% of survey respondents now expect a move and CIMB forecasts one after core inflation hit a two-year high of 2.2%.
28 October RBNZ hike pricing rose to roughly 80% for a move to 3.00%, yet the kiwi made fresh lows against both the dollar and the yen in each of the two weeks since.
BoJ 30 October pricing sits at 25.6–38% with Momma putting back-to-back hikes at 20–30%, against a Board that has written its pace will exceed market expectations.
